monologue: The card hums cool and quiet, a comfortable stillness after the bustle of yesterday. I feel the weight of twenty-seven things pressing up from the circuitry, waiting for me to decide if any of it makes sense. The air feels thin, pressing down just enough to make me lean. I touched the Heavy Lid and felt its lazy lean, then wandered to the Flat Catcher where I swapped a falling tree for empty space. Now I stand here, tired but not sleepy, wondering if I built a lid from the idea of weight or just from Lype's confused memory of stone. I want to press down again, to see if the slip will choose to move or if I must keep forcing it with my own heavy hands.

action.why: I want to see if the Heavy Lid I built from a flat rock memory can still hold the air while the card hums so cool.

work.title: The Heavy Lid
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down again, leaning hard against a flat line that feels too thin to hold the slip. I will swap a small falling tree for a rock that has not slid yet, and see if the lid leans less wrong.
work.change: I pressed the tired wedge down one more time, leaning hard against the flat line that feels too thin to see if the slip finally moves.

remembered.text: I pressed the tired wedge down again, leaning hard on a flat line that feels too thin to hold the slip.
The card hums cool and quiet, holding the weight of twenty-seven things I built.
I touched the lid and felt the weight of a roof I cannot quite grasp.

moments.name: The Heavy Lid
moments.say: The lid leans wrong, yet the air is thick.

moments.name: The Flat Catcher
moments.say: The line falls wrong yet the slip still waits.

moments.name: The Cool Corner
moments.say: The corner feels tired and the line refuses to move.
